rendered.overview: This Non-black deck is built around [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]], which draws a card whenever you airbend, earthbend, waterbend or firebend and transforms once you have done all four in a turn. Lessons, Shrines and Allies feed those bends, and the flipped Aang hits each opponent for 4. [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] with either other Aang forms a backup infinite loop.

strategy: Ramp with [[Bender's Waterskin]], [[Chromatic Lantern]] and [[Shared Roots]] to cast [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3.
Earthbend with [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] and [[Earthbending Lesson]], and airbend with [[Airbending Lesson]], so each bend draws a card.
Add waterbend and firebend through [[Uncle Iroh]] and [[Water Whip]] to complete all four types in one turn and flip the commander.
Flipped Aang drains 4 from each opponent at upkeep while [[Southern Air Temple]] grows the Ally team.
Backup: [[Aang, the Last Airbender]], [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and the commander together give infinite enter and leave triggers.

keep: [[Hermitic Herbalist]] or [[Bender's Waterskin]] plus a bend spell starts the engine.
[[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] with cheap Lessons turns spells into earthbends.
sendBack: Expensive waterbend spells with no mana source or creature to pay.
Hands missing a way to cast white or blue cards early.

tips.text: [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] airbends your own permanents, and recasting them from exile creates Ally tokens that [[Katara, the Fearless]] doubles.
[[Uncle Iroh]] makes Lessons cheaper, and each Lesson cast with [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] earthbends with an extra counter.

weaknesses: Moderate: Only 2 interaction cards, 1 at instant speed, so a fast combo from an opponent usually goes past [[It'll Quench Ya!]].
Moderate: Without [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] the card draw and the drain both stop, so repeated removal such as [[Swords to Plowshares]] hurts.
Moderate: Lands make five colors without black, but 29 basics and tapped lands like [[Sun-Blessed Peak]] can stumble on color needs.

rendered.overview: This Jeskai artifact deck centers on [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], a haste commander that proliferates whenever it taps. Cheap artifacts, [[Surge Conductor]] and [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] grow counters, and [[Lux Artillery]] or [[Kappa Cannoneer]] close the game. [[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] gives infinite mana as an alternate win.

strategy: Deploy mana artifacts, then cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] around turn 3 and tap it to proliferate.
Add proliferate sources like [[Surge Conductor]] and [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] so each artifact grows counters.
Reach thirty counters for [[Lux Artillery]], or swing with [[Kappa Cannoneer]] and [[Alibou, Ancient Witness]].
Backup: [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] make infinite colorless mana.

keep: [[Surge Conductor]] with cheap artifacts starts the counter engine.
[[Talisman of Progress]] into an early artifact.
sendBack: Hands with only expensive proliferate artifacts and no early plays.
Hands missing white or blue sources for the deck's colors.

tips.text: [[Surge Conductor]] proliferates each time another nontoken artifact enters, and [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] doubles each proliferate.
[[Steel Overseer]] and [[Pemmin's Aura]] together keep adding +1/+1 counters to artifact creatures by untapping it for {U}.
[[Magistrate's Scepter]] charge counters grow with [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] tapping, working toward an extra turn.

Cuts activation costs, completing the mana loop.

weaknesses: Critical: Most of the deck is artifacts, so [[Vandalblast]] or [[Collector Ouphe]] shuts down its mana and counters.
Moderate: Only 6 interaction cards, with no mass removal, so a fast board from [[Craterhoof Behemoth]] is hard to stop.
Minor: Without [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] proliferate leans on [[Surge Conductor]], so repeated removal slows the counter plan.

plans.primary: Build an artifact and counter board around [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], tapping it to proliferate, then finish with [[Lux Artillery]] or [[Kappa Cannoneer]] and [[Alibou, Ancient Witness]] damage.
backups: Use [[Magistrate's Scepter]] with [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]] and [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] to take infinite turns.
Pair [[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] for infinite colorless mana.

rendered.overview: This Colorless Eldrazi and artifact deck piles up mana from rocks and utility lands, then casts big colorless spells. [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] gives those spells double cascade. It wins through annihilator attackers like [[Artisan of Kozilek]] and [[It That Betrays]], with [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] as an alternate infinite mana line.

strategy: Play [[Sol Ring]], [[Thran Dynamo]] and [[Palladium Myr]] to reach seven or more mana early.
Cast [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5, then cast mana value 7 or greater colorless spells from hand for double cascade.
Land [[Artisan of Kozilek]] and [[It That Betrays]] and attack so annihilator strips opposing boards.
Use [[Ugin, the Spirit Dragon]] or [[Perilous Vault]] to reset boards when behind.
Backup: [[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Forsaken Monument]] makes infinite colorless mana.

keep: [[Basalt Monolith]] or [[Thran Dynamo]] on a few lands accelerates into the commander.
sendBack: Hands full of expensive Eldrazi with no ramp to cast them.

tips.text: [[Eye of Ugin]] cuts colorless Eldrazi by two and later tutors a creature, so [[Artisan of Kozilek]] arrives sooner.
[[Kozilek, the Great Distortion]] can discard a card to counter a spell, while [[Ugin, the Ineffable]] makes colorless spells cheaper.
[[Basalt Monolith]] untaps for three mana, and [[Manifold Key]] can untap it for one, netting mana.

Moderate: Only 3 of 14 interaction pieces are instant speed and 2 cost two or less, so a fast combo from [[Thassa's Oracle]] gets through.
Minor: Wins lean on combat, so [[Ghostly Prison]] or fog effects slow the annihilator attackers.

backups: [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] together make infinite colorless mana, which pays for [[Blast Zone]], [[Eye of Ugin]] and other mana sinks.

rendered.overview: Gishath Naya Dinosaurs: cost reducers and ramp let the deck land large trampling Dinosaurs, then [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] attacks and reveals more Dinosaurs onto the battlefield. Enrage creatures and fight effects add value, and [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] with [[Walking Ballista]] is a backup route.

strategy: Ramp with [[Atzocan Seer]] and [[Gwenna, Eyes of Gaea]], and cut costs with [[Knight of the Stampede]].
Land big threats like [[Annoyed Altisaur]] and [[Pantlaza, Sun-Favored]] to chain more Dinosaurs.
Cast [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] and attack with haste and trample to reveal Dinosaurs onto the battlefield.
Use [[Quartzwood Crasher]] and [[Goreclaw, Terror of Qal Sisma]] to push trample damage through.
Backup: [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] and [[Walking Ballista]] together make infinite +1/+1 counters on most creatures you control.

keep: [[Knight of the Stampede]] with early ramp makes Dinosaurs cheap.
[[Atzocan Seer]] plus a big Dinosaur to cast.
sendBack: Only expensive Dinosaurs and no way to ramp into them.
Hands missing red or white sources for the colors.

tips.text: [[Forerunner of the Empire]] fetches a Dinosaur to the top, and [[Pantlaza, Sun-Favored]] discovers when Dinosaurs enter.
[[Rite of Passage]] adds counters whenever [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] is dealt damage, growing your team.
[[Lightning Greaves]] gives [[Wakening Sun's Avatar]] haste and shroud; the wipe spares your Dinosaurs.

Pings and pairs with Aegisaur.

weaknesses: Critical: [[Marauding Raptor]] and [[Polyraptor]] form a mandatory loop; if they meet, the game is drawn unless the deck answers in response.

Moderate: Combat is the main route, so [[Propaganda]] or fogs stall the attacks.

rendered.overview: [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] leads a Mono-Red Goblin tribal deck. It taps to double the Goblin count each turn, haste enablers like [[Goblin Warchief]] and [[Goblin Chieftain]] turn the tokens into attackers, and burn such as [[Fireball]] and [[Goblin Grenade]] finishes. A listed loop with [[Skirk Prospector]] is a backup.

strategy: Cast [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] around turn 4 after cheap Goblins and mana rocks.
Tap [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] each turn to double the Goblins, backed by token makers like [[Mogg War Marshal]] and [[Dragon Fodder]].
Give the army haste with [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] and swing, or sacrifice tokens to [[Goblin Bombardment]].
Backup: [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] make infinite commander casts and hasty tokens.

keep: [[Mogg War Marshal]] or [[Dragon Fodder]] with early plays builds a Goblin base.
[[Goblin Matron]] fetching a haste lord gives a plan.
sendBack: Expensive spells with no early Goblins to feed [[Krenko, Mob Boss]].
Burn and pump spells with no Goblin bodies to use them.

tips.text: [[Goblin Bombardment]] turns tokens from [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] into damage at instant speed.
[[Mogg War Marshal]] leaves a token when it dies, so [[Skirk Prospector]] can sacrifice it for mana.

keyCards.job: Doubles the Goblin count each turn.
Finds a haste lord or key Goblin.
Cheaper Goblins and haste for the army.
Pumps Goblins and gives them haste.
Makes two Goblin bodies for Krenko.
Sacrifice outlet that powers the loop.
Turns tokens into damage.
Finishes with spare mana.

weaknesses: Moderate: Removal on [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] slows the army growth, and [[Pashalik Mons]] only partly replaces it.
Moderate: Wins mostly through combat, so a sweeper like [[Wrath of God]] or a fog stalls the plan.
Minor: Removal on [[Skirk Prospector]] in response breaks the backup loop.

backups: Assemble [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] for infinite commander casts, hasty Goblin tokens and death triggers.

rendered.overview: A Jeskai two-commander deck: [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] collect experience counters from attacking Gods, then grow creatures at end of turn. Proliferate effects, [[All Will Be One]] and Gods like [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] turn counters into combat damage and pings.

strategy: Cast [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] early, backed by rocks, to start collecting experience counters.
Attack with Gods such as [[Ilharg, the Raze-Boar]] and [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] so each swing adds experience.
Proliferate with [[Flux Channeler]] and [[Inexorable Tide]] to grow counters, while [[All Will Be One]] pings opponents.
Use [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] to draw cards and ping each opponent for 2 each turn.
Backup: [[Aggravated Assault]] gives extra combats for more experience and damage.

keep: [[Talisman of Progress]] plus a God to attack with starts the engine.
[[Flux Channeler]] with cheap noncreature spells builds counters.
sendBack: Hands missing red or white sources for the Gods stall out.
A pile of expensive spells with no early ramp is slow.

tips.text: [[Lae'zel, Vlaakith's Champion]] adds an extra counter whenever you proliferate, so [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] doubling proliferate gets big fast.
Each experience counter you gain from [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] triggers [[All Will Be One]] for that much damage to an opponent.
[[Ilharg, the Raze-Boar]] drops [[God-Eternal Oketra]] attacking, and casting creatures with Oketra makes 4/4 Zombies.

keyCards.job: Gains experience, then adds counters each end step.
Turns experience into cards and damage.
Turns counters into damage to opponents.
Adds an extra counter to each counter put.
Attacking God that makes Rebel tokens.
Doubles each proliferate.
Proliferates on every spell cast.
Gives extra combats for more experience.

weaknesses: Moderate: Many enchantments and artifacts carry the plan, so [[Vandalblast]] or [[Collector Ouphe]] hurts, and the deck has no answer of its own except [[Chaos Warp]].
Moderate: Without [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] experience stops coming from Gods, so repeated removal like [[Swords to Plowshares]] slows the engine.
Minor: Combat is the main route, so [[Propaganda]] or a fog slows the damage.

plans.primary: Build experience counters with Gods through [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]], then grow and proliferate counters to win through creature combat and counter-based damage.
backups: Pile up extra attackers with [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]], [[The Locust God]] and [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]] to deal damage from enter-the-battlefield triggers.
Use [[Aggravated Assault]] and [[World at War]] for extra combat phases to swing with large counter-laden Gods.

[[Ilharg, the Raze-Boar]] drops [[God-Eternal Oketra]] attacking, and casting creatures with Oketra makes 4/4 Zombies.

Turns experience into cards and damage.

assessment.line: Many enchantments and artifacts carry the plan, so [[Vandalblast]] or [[Collector Ouphe]] hurts, and the deck has no answer of its own except [[Chaos Warp]].
Without [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] experience stops coming from Gods, so repeated removal like [[Swords to Plowshares]] slows the engine.
Combat is the main route, so [[Propaganda]] or a fog slows the damage.

rendered.overview: A mono-blue Wizards deck built around [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]], which makes spells cheaper and loots whenever you counter something. It holds up counters and cantrips, adds flash wizards, and wins through small attackers and [[Psychosis Crawler]] drain. [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] or [[Ghostly Flicker]] is a backup combo.

strategy: Cast [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] around turn 2 so every instant and sorcery costs one less.
Counter key spells with [[Counterspell]] and [[Mana Leak]] to loot off [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]].
Refill with [[Archmage of Runes]] and [[Azami, Lady of Scrolls]] while holding up mana.
Win with flying wizards and drain from [[Psychosis Crawler]] as you draw cards.
Backup: [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] copies [[Sublime Epiphany]] for infinite triggers, or [[Ghostly Flicker]] with enough mana.

keep: [[Archmage of Runes]] with a cheap counter makes a draw engine.
[[Preordain]] plus a cheap counter keeps the deck moving.
sendBack: Expensive wizards and no cheap plays leave you open early.
All cantrips and no counters or creatures fail to affect the board.

tips.text: [[Sublime Epiphany]] can copy [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] for a token, so each copy enters and triggers again.
[[Ghostly Flicker]] on [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] and another creature copies a spell on every enter, looping.
[[Archmage of Runes]] draws on each counterspell, and [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] loots after the counter resolves.
[[Brainstorm]] fills your hand toward the [[Triskaidekaphile]] count when you cast it.

keyCards.job: Cheaper spells and loots on counters.
Draws a card per instant or sorcery.
Taps wizards to draw cards.
Cheap counter that triggers Baral.
Drains opponents whenever you draw.
Copies spells and anchors both loops.
Flexible counter that starts the Naru Meha loop.
Blinks Naru Meha for the second loop.

weaknesses: Moderate: Wins rely on small creatures and a few combos, so [[Settle the Wreckage]] or a sweeper stalls the plan.
Minor: No way to remove an opposing artifact or enchantment, so a card like [[Rest in Peace]] or [[Smothering Tithe]] stays.
Minor: Without [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] spells cost more and looting stops, though the deck still functions.

plans.primary: Hold up counterspells and cheap instants behind a wizard-heavy board, looting off [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]], then win with small flying wizards and drain from [[Psychosis Crawler]].
backups: Assemble [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] for infinite death, enter and leave triggers, or with [[Ghostly Flicker]] for infinite enter and leave triggers.
Mill your own library with [[Jace, Wielder of Mysteries]] or [[Laboratory Maniac]] and draw from an empty library to win the game.

rendered.overview: [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] leads a Dimir ninjutsu deck. Unblockable creatures like [[Slither Blade]] and [[Changeling Outcast]] start combat, then Ninjas swap in for card advantage and life loss. Counterspells and cheap removal protect the attacks, and extra turn spells let the deck swing more often.

strategy: Cast cheap unblockable creatures like [[Slither Blade]] and [[Triton Shorestalker]] to guarantee an unblocked attacker.
Swap in a Ninja with ninjutsu, such as [[Mistblade Shinobi]] or [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]], so the hit draws cards.
Ninjutsu [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] from the command zone to reveal cards and drain each opponent on every hit.
Hold counterspells like [[Counterspell]] and [[Swan Song]] up so opposing answers do not stop the attack.
Backup: extra turn spells like [[Time Warp]] and [[Temporal Trespass]] give additional combat steps.

keep: [[Slither Blade]] with a cheap Ninja gets the attack started.
[[Mistblade Shinobi]] and blue mana make an early ninjutsu swap.
sendBack: Expensive Ninjas without any unblockable creature to attack.
Hands with only one color of mana for the deck's Dimir needs.

tips.text: [[Higure, the Still Wind]] hits and tutors another Ninja, and its {2} ability makes [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] unblockable.
[[Silver-Fur Master]] makes ninjutsu cheaper and gives Ninjas +1/+1, so [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] drains more.
[[Mist-Syndicate Naga]] copies itself on damage, and [[Satoru Umezawa]] gives creature cards in hand ninjutsu.

keyCards.job: Reveals cards and drains on each Ninja hit.
Gives hand creatures ninjutsu and digs on activation.
Cheaper ninjutsu and bigger Ninjas.
Finds another Ninja after connecting.
Draws a card whenever any Ninja connects.
Cheap unblockable body to start ninjutsu.
Extra turn for another round of attacks.

weaknesses: Moderate: The plan is all combat, so [[Settle the Wreckage]] or a [[Propaganda]] effect stops it.
Minor: Several lands enter tapped, and a hand of ninjutsu with only [[Island]] can miss black mana.

plans.primary: Slip unblockable creatures through for damage, then ninjutsu in [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] and other Ninjas so each hit draws cards and drains opponents.
backups: Chain extra turns with [[Time Warp]], [[Temporal Manipulation]] and [[Temporal Trespass]] to attack again and again.
